key_insight: Biasing initialization toward stiff, flat hinges helps gradient-based origami design avoid physically unfavorable basins and improves success after discretization.
engineering_relevance: A no-extra-compute initialization change can improve discrete mechanical designs, while penalties targeting geometric incompatibility and floppiness offer further gains.
method: Use automatic differentiation in bilevel optimization to assign four discrete hinge types on fixed origami geometries.
Bias the continuous relaxation’s initialization toward the stiff, flat hinge option.
Alternatively, penalize frustration and floppiness in the outer design loss.
evidence_signal: Relaxed optimization solved 97% of baseline runs, but discrete success was 49%; the initialization prior raised discrete success to 69%, and physical penalties raised it to 78%.
watch_item: The reported gains concern fixed-geometry origami design; transfer to other discrete mechanical systems remains to be established.
paper_title: Physically Interpretable Basin Selection in Discrete-Variable Origami Design
